title: Computers and Words 💬

mascot.name: Chip
mascot.greeting: Hi, it's Chip! How does a chat app write back to you? Let's find out how computers work with words!

recap: A computer cuts sentences into tokens and gives each a number.
Words that mean similar things sit close on a word map.
Chat apps write by guessing the next word, again and again.

sections.heading: 1. Cutting Words into Pieces
sections.bigIdea: A computer cuts sentences into small pieces and gives each one a number.
sections.chipQuote: I can't read like you. I need words in small pieces!

analogy.description: To see how a brick model is made, you take it apart, one brick at a time.

sections.bodyMarkdown:
A computer can't read the way you do. First it cuts your sentence into small pieces called **tokens**. A token can be a whole word, like "dog". It can be part of a word, like "ing".

Each token gets its own number. Now the computer can work with the sentence.

jargonBuster.simpleExplanation: The small pieces a computer cuts words into. Each one gets a number.

diagram.caption: From a sentence to numbers
diagram.alt: Three steps: a sentence, the sentence cut into pieces, and each piece given a number.
steps: Cut into pieces: I | am | jump | ing ✂️

teen.add: Cutting words into parts helps with new words. Even if the computer never saw "unjumpable", it knows "un", "jump" and "able".

checkIn.question: What does a computer do first with your sentence?
checkIn.praise: Yes! It cuts it into tokens.
checkIn.explanation: A computer first cuts a sentence into tokens and gives each one a number.

sections.heading: 2. A Map of Words
sections.bigIdea: Words that mean similar things sit close together on a map.
sections.chipQuote: Puppy and dog are best friends on my map!

analogy.description: At lunch, friends sit together. The football fans share one table. The chess club shares another.

sections.bodyMarkdown:
A token's number alone says nothing about meaning. So the computer puts each word on a big **word map**. Words used in the same way end up close together.

"Puppy" sits near "dog". "Apple" sits near "banana". But "dog" and "banana" are far apart.

jargonBuster.simpleExplanation: A map where words with similar meanings sit close together.

diagram.caption: Close words sit together
diagram.content:
graph LR
    subgraph Pets ["🐾 Pets corner"]
        Dog["dog"] --- Puppy["puppy"]
    end
    subgraph Fruit ["🍎 Fruit corner"]
        Apple["apple"] --- Banana["banana"]
    end
diagram.alt: Two corners of a word map. Dog and puppy sit together in the pets corner. Apple and banana sit together in the fruit corner, far from the pets.

teen.add: Each word's spot is a list of numbers called an **embedding**. You can even do maths with them. King minus man plus woman lands near queen.

jargonBuster.simpleExplanation: A list of numbers that gives a word its spot on the word map.

interactiveWidget.title: 🗺️ Try It: The Word Map
interactiveWidget.instruction: Tap an example. See where the words land, and which ones are close.
interactiveWidget.goal: Find which words sit close together on the map of meaning.
interactiveWidget.predictionPrompt: Before you tap: which two words do you think sit closest?
hints: Words used in similar ways end up near each other.
Try the king and queen example.
interactiveWidget.successMessage: You read the word map! Computers place similar words close together.

sections.heading: 3. The Next-Word Game
sections.bigIdea: Chat apps write by guessing the next word, again and again.
sections.chipQuote: Happy birth... You already know the next word, don't you?

analogy.description: Your friend says "Happy birth..." and you shout "day!" You guessed from the words before.

sections.bodyMarkdown:
Chat apps learned from a huge amount of writing. Give one the words "The cat sat on the". It works out which next word is most likely, like "mat" or "sofa".

It adds that word and guesses again. Word by word, it builds a whole answer. It is good at guessing, but it can still be wrong.

diagram.caption: How a chat app writes
diagram.alt: Four steps: read the words so far, guess the most likely next word, add it, and repeat until the answer is done.
steps: Read the words so far: "The cat sat on the" 📖
Guess the most likely next word: "mat" 🤔
Add it: "The cat sat on the mat" ➕
Guess again, until the answer is done. 🔁

teen.add: Most chat apps today use a design called a **transformer**. It looks back at all the words so far and picks out which ones matter most for the next guess.

jargonBuster.simpleExplanation: A design for language AI that looks at all the words so far to guess the next one.

checkIn.question: How does a chat app build its answer?
options: 🔁 One guessed word at a time
checkIn.explanation: A chat app guesses the next word, adds it, and guesses again.

sections.heading: 4. Word Helpers Everywhere
sections.bigIdea: Language AI helps you every day.
sections.chipQuote: Words are everywhere, so word helpers are too!

analogy.description: On holiday, you point your phone at a menu. It tells you what the food is, in your own language.

sections.bodyMarkdown:
Your phone can read a sign in another language and say it in yours. Your email hides junk messages. A voice helper sets a timer when you ask it to.

All of these cut words into tokens and use a word map. Chat apps can sound sure even when they are wrong. So check facts that matter.

diagram.caption: Where language AI helps
diagram.content:
graph TD
    W["💬 Language AI"] --> T["🌐 Translating signs"]
    W --> S["🛡️ Hiding junk email"]
    W --> V["🎙️ Voice helpers"]
    W --> C["🤖 Chat apps"]
diagram.alt: Language AI helps with translating signs, hiding junk email, voice helpers and chat apps.

teen.add: A chat app can make up facts that sound real. This is because it predicts likely words, not true ones. Always check important facts with a trusted source.

checkIn.question: A chat app tells you a fact for your homework. What should you do?
checkIn.praise: Yes! Chat apps can be wrong.
checkIn.explanation: Chat apps can sound sure and still be wrong, so check facts that matter.

miniQuiz.praise: Yes! Similar words sit close together.
miniQuiz.explanation: Words with similar meanings sit close together on the word map.
